title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Ava Martinez
description: Fixes several interrelated SSE streaming issues that caused truncated/duplicated partial JSON payloads and incorrect delimiter/token ordering in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: customers observed malformed partial JSON events when streaming high-frequency tool/function-calling outputs and when content included closing braces or text resembling delimiters. This caused downstream JSON parser errors in SDKs and client integrations. The PR standardizes chunk boundary handling, enforces deterministic event ordering for token and meta events, and hardens delimiter escape detection. Key changes: 1) Reworked chunk assembler to keep an internal state machine that distinguishes token fragments, partial JSON objects, and SSE event boundaries; 2) Introduced explicit buffer flush rules on boundary conditions to avoid emitting half-objects as complete events; 3) Normalized ordering guarantees so 'meta' events (e.g. function call start/finish, structured-output markers) are emitted before any trailing token events for the same logical message; 4) Improved OpenAI-compat adapter to add safe escaping for payloads that contain SSE delimiter substrings and to collapse consecutive delimiter-like sequences; 5) Added a configurable "sse.strictDelimiter" flag (default=false) to preserve backward compatibility while allowing stricter framing for new customers. Testing and rollout: unit tests for assembler state transitions, fuzz tests reproducing reported truncation patterns, and an integration smoke test against python/js SDKs. Rolling strategy: feature gated behind sse.strictDelimiter=false by default; Gradual rollout to hosted API then Dedicated, monitoring for parser errors and latency regressions. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged; enabling strictDelimiter is opt-in. See release_notes for more details.
